stories.title: How Silence Became a Weapon in World War II
stories.description: A real WWII tactic where doing nothing on the radio misled enemy intelligence.

scenes.visual_prompt: Wide cinematic establishing shot of a foggy European battlefield at dawn, abandoned radio equipment in the foreground, muted colors, slow cinematic camera drift
scenes.negative_prompt: text, watermark, logo, modern objects, cartoon
scenes.narration: How did complete radio silence confuse enemy armies during World War Two?

scenes.visual_prompt: Quiet military command tent at night, radios powered on but untouched, indicator lights glowing faintly, canvas gently moving in the wind
scenes.narration: German intelligence closely tracked Allied radio signals to predict every major move.

scenes.visual_prompt: Allied radio operators sitting still with hands away from controls, ticking clocks, shadows stretching across detailed military maps
scenes.narration: Then, without warning, entire Allied units stopped transmitting altogether.

scenes.visual_prompt: Montage of enemy analysts listening to static-filled radios, confused expressions, maps showing misplaced troop expectations
scenes.narration: The silence itself became the signal, convincing the enemy that a massive attack was being hidden elsewhere.

scenes.visual_prompt: Quiet wide shot of radios sitting unused as the sun rises over a calm battlefield, reflective mood, slow fade feeling
scenes.narration: In war, even silence can be carefully planned—and incredibly powerful.
